prompt: Set up logging for the new payment service. What should I use?
output:
Your team already adopted **structured logging with correlation IDs** across all services — match that pattern. Given your Kotlin + EKS stack, here's what to use:

**Logger: [Logback](https://logback.qos.ch/) + [logstash-logback-encoder](https://github.com/logfellow/logstash-logback-encoder)**

This is the standard for Kotlin/JVM on Kubernetes — outputs JSON natively, plays well with whatever log aggregation you're using (Datadog, CloudWatch, etc.).

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
implementation("net.logstash.logback:logstash-logback-encoder:7.4")
```

```xml
<!-- logback.xml -->
<appender name="JSON" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
  <encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder"/>
</appender>
```

```kotlin
// Usage — always pass correlation ID and payment context as structured fields
private val log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(PaymentService::class.java)

log.info("payment_initiated",
    kv("correlation_id", correlationId),
    kv("payment_id", paymentId),
    kv("amount_cents", amountCents),
    kv("merchant_id", merchantId)
)
```

**Key points for a payment service specifically:**
- Propagate `correlation_id` from the incoming gRPC metadata — thread it through every log call
- Log `payment_id`, `merchant_id`, and `amount_cents` (not amount as float) as structured fields on every relevant log line
- Use `WARN` for retryable failures, `ERROR` for non-retryable — keeps alerting clean
- Never log card numbers, CVVs, or full account numbers — mask to last 4

This stays consistent with your other services and keeps dependencies minimal — no new infrastructure needed.
